# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48 (Bi-Vb Pc48)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc48
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48
**Title (English, from literature):** Not relinquishing a lodging
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48, entitled *Āvasathavihāra* ("Not relinquishing a lodging"), is a monastic disciplinary rule in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka concerning the proper maintenance and surrender of residential quarters. The rule establishes that a nun who departs on tour without formally relinquishing or handing over her dwelling incurs an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the nuns' legal corpus, Ute Hüsken notes that *āvasatha* is employed here much like *upassaya* ("dwelling" or "residence") and highlights the formal similarity between this rule and Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 47; both rules require items or lodgings after personal use to be officially handed over to fellow monastic members to guarantee their continued proper upkeep [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken also observes that this specific prohibition, which prevents nuns from vacating lodgings without entrusting them to someone else, has no direct parallel applied to monks [Hüsken 1997]. Modern translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Text-reuse algorithms in DharmaNexus corroborate cross-language alignments with Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* passages and Tibetan Vinaya materials, including the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D 5) and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D 4106) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 306 shared segments with 84 texts, reflecting extensive Vinaya legal and stock phraseology shared with Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 47 (§1.14–2.1.5), Saṅghādisesa 3, and several other Bhikkhunī Pācittiya rules [DharmaNexus].
